_comment: Which CI job collects which test-id namespace (#313).
The ledger's evidence check (C3) compares each cited test against an
inventory of what a lane collected, and a lane only speaks for the
namespaces it declares — so an id in a namespace *no* lane covers was
skipped by every lane and silently accepted. Demonstrated: a claim
passed the GUI lane with 'CAPABILITY LEDGER OK'.
validate_capabilities.py --lanes checks every cited id against this
map, which needs no test run, and each lane asserts its own row
against what it actually collected so the map cannot drift into
A namespace is a prefix of a test id, and it has to be no broader than what the lane really runs: 'tests/' would vouch for every path under it, including one nothing collects.

Each lane declares runs_on_every_revision. A lane that does not run on every revision can have evidence older than the code being released, so --release-revision refuses to certify a release with claims resting on such a lane unless its evidence was recorded at that exact revision. The field is required: a new lane cannot slip in as trustworthy by omitting it.

lanes.collects: nextest JUnit for the whole Rust workspace
lanes.excludes_reason: These targets need LibreOffice installed. This lane does not have it, and without REQUIRE_SOFFICE the tests return early and report *ok* — measured: with no soffice on PATH, we_read_soffice_output prints 'skipping: soffice not installed' and nextest records a pass. A crate-level namespace would therefore let this lane offer those passes as live evidence for a claim only the oracle lane can support.

lanes.collects: pytest collection of the AT-SPI journeys
pytest collection of the validator and harness tests it names
the LibreOffice oracle and the LibreOffice-authored parity corpus
lanes.runs_on_every_revision_reason: Scheduled daily, plus pull requests that touch format or model code. Neither guarantees a run at the revision being released: the schedule sees whatever main was at 05:00, and the path filter sees nothing at all when a release changes only packaging.
